activity.notes: ATLAS uses c.1400 as an explicitly approximate representative scholarly-activity point: MacTutor places Madhava's discovery of the sine, cosine and arctangent series around 1400. This is not an exact birth, death, or composition date. The conventional Sangamagrama-near-Cochin localization is used only for the broad historical polity association and is not treated as proof of an exact birthplace.

sources.title: Madhava (1350–1425) — MacTutor History of Mathematics
sources.citation_text: MacTutor describes Madhava as a south Indian mathematician from Sangamagrama near Cochin and dates his trigonometric infinite-series discoveries to around 1400.

sources.title: Cochin State Manual (1911) — Government of Kerala
sources.citation_text: The Cochin State Manual records the historical kingdom of Perumpadappu or Cochin as a Kerala polity; ATLAS uses this as polity-identity support rather than as evidence for Madhava's exact locality.
